original_question: Does there exist a non-uniform Eberlein compact space K such that C(K) belongs to the class U of Banach spaces for which every Pettis integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is McShane integrable? Equivalently, are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K = {K : C(K) ∈ U}?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.7 in §3.3: “Are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K?” Here U is the class of Banach spaces X such that every Pettis integrable function f:[0,1]→X is McShane integrable, and K is the class of compacta K with C(K)∈U. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly asks for the existence of a non-uniform Eberlein compact space K with C(K) in the class U, and it also correctly restates the problem in terms of the class of compacta K={K:C(K)∈U}. That is exactly the content of Problem 3.7 once the surrounding notation from §3.3 is unpacked. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s standing conventions are that all topological spaces are Hausdorff and all Banach spaces are real; making those conventions explicit helps the question stand alone. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
To make the question self-contained, C(K) should be identified as the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K, with the supremum norm.

The definition of U should be stated explicitly: U={X: every Pettis integrable f:[0,1]→X is McShane integrable}. In the paper, [0,1] is understood with Lebesgue measure by the standing notation. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

The term “Eberlein compact” is implicit in your draft and should be spelled out if full self-containment is desired: K is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

The term “uniform Eberlein compact” should also be made explicit: K is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of a Hilbert space; equivalently, C(K) is Hilbert generated. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

If one uses the compact-space class notation, that class should be defined explicitly as 𝒦={L compact Hausdorff : C(L)∈U}; otherwise the symbol K is overloaded between the compact space and the class of compacta. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let U be the class of real Banach spaces X such that every Pettis integrable function f:[0,1]→X (with [0,1] equipped with Lebesgue measure) is McShane integrable, and let 𝒦:= {L compact Hausdorff : C(L)∈U}, where C(L) denotes the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on L with the supremum norm. Does there exist a compact Hausdorff space K such that K is Eberlein (i.e. homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space), K is not uniform Eberlein (i.e. not homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of any Hilbert space), and C(K) belongs to U? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the McShane-integral open problem in §3.3, not a broader neighboring question. The surrounding text first defines the class U, then defines the associated class of compacta K with C(K)∈U, notes that this class contains every uniform Eberlein compact but not every Eberlein compact, and finally states Problem 3.7 asking exactly whether there are non-uniform Eberlein compacta in that class. The refined version therefore keeps the scope unchanged and only makes explicit the paper’s hidden conventions and the definitions of Eberlein/uniform Eberlein needed for a stand-alone formulation. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
